title: Taste & Craft: A Conversation with Tuomas Artman, CTO Linear & Gergely Orosz, @The Pragmatic Engineer
talk_summary: Tuomas Artman (CTO Linear) argues that when agents make shipping cheap, the scarce resource becomes taste and quality, not code volume. He describes concrete mechanisms: a zero-bug policy, weekly 'quality Wednesdays' where every engineer must self-find one fix, and routing trivial bug fixes to single-shot AI.

takeaways.what_they_do: Every reported bug is auto-assigned to the person who touched that area and becomes their top priority; they may decline if gnarly/rare, but the backlog is never allowed to accumulate. They cleared the existing backlog in ~3 weeks of feature freeze, then held the line.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if a bug gets reported um it gets assigned to somebody automatically immediately using agents
takeaways.numbers: 3 weeks feature freeze to reach zero; bugs then fixed within 7 days, usually 2-3 hours

takeaways.technique: Quality Wednesdays: each engineer self-finds one quality fix weekly
takeaways.what_they_do: Weekly 30-min all-hands where every engineer demos one small quality fix they found themselves (not a filed bug). Because they must find one each week, they stay tuned to quality while doing unrelated work, which reduces new regressions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you have to every Wednesday you have to find a problem yourself like we won't hand them to you
takeaways.numbers: ~25 engineers in ~37 min; 2,500-3,000 small fixes to date; 35 problems found in one tiny menu

takeaways.technique: Single-shot AI for trivial bug fixes
takeaways.what_they_do: A slice of incoming bugs are fixed end-to-end by a single-shot AI instance that opens and lands a PR with no engineer involvement; they expect this share to grow toward 100% for low-thinking tasks.
takeaways.evidence_quote: 10% of our bugs are automatically fixed by you know a singleshot AI instance
takeaways.numbers: 10% of bugs auto-fixed and landed with no engineer

takeaways.technique: Say no / root-cause grouping of feature requests
takeaways.what_they_do: They never ship customer feature requests as stated; they cluster requests, find the root problem, and design one solution for the group. AI summarizes requests but humans decide what to build.

takeaways.technique: Expose agents to raw customer signal
takeaways.what_they_do: Open Slack channels with big customers and recorded/tagged customer calls are searchable by everyone, so engineers constantly see real customer pain rather than specs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you get this like fire hose of like what are customers feedback

takeaways.technique: Agents lack taste/time perception; human polish pass on UX
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues agents can produce animations/UI but pick wrong easing/duration because they have no felt sense of time; a human designer's small manual pass makes it feel natural.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it doesn't know whether two seconds is is is slow enough
